title: GPU lane enforcement and proactive noisy-neighbor detection for Dedicated capacity
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Implement a lane-based enforcement layer and proactive noisy-neighbor detection to provide throughput guarantees and quota enforcement on Dedicated GPU capacity. This ticket covers design, runtime controls, monitoring, and a staged rollout for the isolation primitives that prevent a tenant from degrading co-tenants' SLOs. Workstreams include enforcement primitives (lane throttles, soft reservations), detection heuristics (KV/attn pressure, GPU SM saturation patterns), autoscaler integration (backpressure signals for policy-aware scaling), and operator tooling (eviction playbook, tenant pausing). The goal is to reduce 95th/99th percentile tail latency regressions caused by noisy tenants while preserving cost efficiency for bursty workloads.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New lane enforcement policy applied to a test pool prevents a noisy synthetic tenant from increasing co-tenant p99 latency by >10% under sustained load. 2) Noisy-neighbor detector flags offending tenants with >=90% precision/recall on labeled replay workloads. 3) Autoscaler receives and respects backpressure signals without thrashing (less than 2 scale events per minute in synthetic tests). 4) Dashboard surfaces per-tenant lane usage, burst credits, and enforced throttles. 5) Rollout plan and rollback tested in staging and approved by SRE and Product.
implementation_summary: Phase 1: Add lane metadata to scheduler and expose soft-reservation tokens per-tenant (+ lease timeout). Instrument GPU metrics (SM utilization, memory bandwidth, queue depth) and KV cache pressure counters for upstream detection. Phase 2: Implement detector service that consumes metrics, computes an anomaly score, and issues enforcement actions (throttle/gently-evict/mark-for-manual). Phase 3: Integrate with autoscaler to translate enforcement state into scaling decisions and with billing to reflect throttled requests. Phase 4: Run canary in dedicated staging pool and measure impact. Phase 5: Gradual rollout with A/B lanes and automated rollback hooks.
tradeoffs: - Strict hard-slicing gives the strongest isolation but wastes capacity for bursty tenants; we choose soft reservations with burst credits to balance utilization. - Detection sensitivity: aggressive thresholds reduce noisy neighbors faster but risk false positives; we'll iterate thresholds using replayed workloads and labeled incidents. - Eviction vs. throttling: eviction is last-resort (customer disruption); first use throttling and reduced concurrency to maintain progress.
test_plan: - Unit tests for lane metadata and lease expiry. - Integration test: multi-tenant replay with controlled noisy workload and golden metrics. - Stress test: 24h soak with mixed traffic and verify autoscaler stability. - Chaos test: simulate node loss and ensure lane enforcement recovers state.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal canary in staging (1 week) 2) Small production pool (5% of dedicated fleet) with monitoring and manual watch 3) Expand to 25% if p99 improvement validated 4) Full fleet rollout with feature flag toggles and automated rollback on regressions.
communication_plan: Notify customers in Dedicated beta group and CS two weeks before prod enablement. Postmortem/FAQ to be published if false positives occur. Run a webinar for platform/solutions engineering covering new throttles and remediation flows.
